An increasing number of data centers are being delayed by permitting issues, and in some instances falling through.

tech.title: How to Formalize All of Mathematics
tech.summary: It would be a terrible waste of resources to spend millions of dollars to formalize mathematics results in libraries nobody uses. Doing so could also disincentivize good research and productive use of AI, disrupt the social norms and practices research depends on, and set the field back decades. Several projects are now working to ensure formal libraries fulfill the community's mathematical goals. Within the next few years, most of mathematics will be able to be formalized in such a way that mathematicians can explore, build on, and make use of formal libraries. This will significantly extend their ability to develop and discover new mathematics.

tech.summary: Researchers have discovered a signal deep in the brain that richly represents a stimulus people are unaware of. This finding makes it possible to understand how a pattern of neural activity accesses consciousness. There are clear signals that correspond to both what is and isn't conscious. This makes it possible to follow both sets of footprints and track down the full machine for generating conscious percepts.

tech.summary: Good products carry something of the people who make them. The difference is how each team understands what they see and the style they go about building it. The founder background or company DNA shapes this a lot.

tech.title: Decoherence
tech.summary: Decoherence is the accumulation of locally valid but mutually incompatible or redundant models within a system. It causes the cost of change to be dominated by translating among those models and preventing unintended side-effects. Decoherence grows relative to the rate of change of a system, and it increases faster the more decoherent a system is, resulting in runaway exponential growth. It rules out the specter of runaway recursive self-improvement, as decoherence both prevents AI from improving in a bubble and limits the rate at which it can improve outside of it. However, it also introduces a new kind of disaster called Decoherence Collapse.

tech.title: Will it be a golden age or a dark age for mathematics (and science)?
tech.summary: Large language models have demonstrated remarkable abilities in generating mathematical proofs. This could lead to a golden age where a new generation of scientists is empowered, new STEM expertise is developed, and an open, collaborative, and intellectually independent scientific enterprise is preserved. However, it could also lead to independent human scientific activity progressively weakening, the production of new knowledge becoming increasingly concentrated in a small number of hands, and knowledge becoming alien to human understanding. The future will likely be a combination of these scenarios.

tech.title: Why One of the World's Greatest Mathematicians Is on a ‘War Footing'
tech.summary: Terence Tao, one of the world's greatest living mathematicians, is currently doing very little math. OpenAI's recent finding in the mathematical field has left him feeling used, as he previously had a good relationship with many employees at the company. Now, he sees them as only using math to evaluate their models, and can't see a way to constructively engage. Despite OpenAI's releases, most problems at the frontiers of math are unsolved, and as math remains infinite, the difficulty of problems is boundless.

In a sample run of 300 streaming requests with up to 200 open at once, five environments consumed 4.75 seconds of CPU. Billing covers active CPU, memory, and requests, so waiting on a database or API uses little CPU but still incurs other charges.

webdev.title: HybridAgent Thinks in Latent Space and Acts in Text
webdev.summary: HybridAgent is a research approach for training AI agents to reason internally using numerical representations instead of writing out every intermediate thought, while still producing text to call tools such as Python or web search and deliver answers. In tests, a 14B Qwen3 model trained this way scored 52.4 on GAIA versus 43.7 for a matched text-only agent, with estimated decoding costs falling from $470 to $176 per million questions.

webdev.title: Someone Behind the Software
webdev.summary: Good products reflect a shared point of view shaped by experience, customer conversations, and judgment. When teams use agents to add features independently, individually useful changes can weaken the product's coherence unless someone keeps shaping the whole.

webdev.title: What Requirements Don't You Have?
webdev.summary: Elegant systems often gain simplicity and scale by accepting limits on freshness, coordination, or flexibility. Coding agents tend to invent extra requirements, so explicitly stating which compromises are acceptable can prevent unnecessary locks, checks, and layers of abstraction.

webdev.title: Does Ruby on Rails Still Make Sense?
webdev.summary: Frameworks remain useful when agents write the code because they supply structure, shared maintenance, and familiar abstractions. Rewriting an application in a faster language can change behavior that users rely on, making targeted optimization and dependency updates a more practical starting point. Familiar code also makes it easier to review the decisions an agent makes.

These signals identify useful pages and filter out nonexistent or duplicated content, which reduces unnecessary crawling load for site owners. Cloudflare states the metadata is used for search discovery rather than training AI models.

devops.title: Finding (and Fixing) a Silent Throughput Ceiling in PostgreSQL

data.title: Under the hood, off the hot path: How D1 scales to millions of databases
data.summary: Cloudflare's D1 serverless SQLite platform keeps query traffic at the edge while its control plane manages millions of tenant databases. Lifecycle operations use idempotent, recoverable flows, with Postgres for transactional metadata, edge KV for routing, and queues for eventually consistent work. The transferable design is to isolate central coordination from the data path so provisioning failures can be repaired without slowing queries.

data.title: A Graph Has No Centre
data.summary: Graph tools for MCP should return focused, bounded views instead of dumping broad subgraphs and hoping prompts impose structure later. The key design move is to make scope explicit in the server through named views, validation rules, and controlled navigation points. For changing entities like avatars, modeling location over time preserves auditability and keeps behavior consistent across clients.

data.title: Which LLM should run your agentic analytics? Accuracy vs. cost of Claude, Gemini and GPT
data.summary: Opus delivered the best analytics reports but cost more. Routing by task balances quality and cost: Sonnet for metrics and trends, Gemini Flash for guided analysis with human review, and Opus for root cause investigations.

data.title: Data Engineering Is the Cache Invalidation Problem Ft. Josh Wills
data.summary: Large Spark and Ray jobs offer the wrong feedback loop for autonomous coding: errors and cost often appear only after hours of distributed execution. Data engineers remain responsible for the materialization choices and failure cases agents cannot evaluate cheaply. The practical response is not blind generation, but representative tests, cost-aware guardrails, and human review where pipelines lack fast feedback.

data.title: The Self-Organizing Data Stack
data.summary: Autonomous data platforms need stable logical assets, not fragile table-and-DAG definitions. This proposed architecture keeps consumer contracts and semantic definitions persistent while a runtime synthesizes, consolidates, verifies, and atomically rewires physical pipelines as needs change. Its strongest safeguard is independent verification against business invariants, plus escalation whenever meaning is ambiguous. Language models may draft changes, but cannot authorize them.

data.title: Differential storage for DuckDB
data.summary: duckdb-differential brings version-control-style workflows to DuckDB, adding snapshots, time travel, branches, clones, and restore through SQL. The core idea is to preserve known-good database states so teams can test imports, run experiments, and reproduce reports without copying entire databases. Shared immutable chunks keep versions efficient, while optional S3 publishing extends those states for remote access and recovery.

data.title: Introducing Timestral
data.summary: Mistral's Timestral models forecast multiple related time series, estimate uncertainty, and incorporate known future inputs such as production schedules. They run on CPUs without task-specific training, and Mistral reports that its largest model, with 209 million parameters, outperforms larger rivals across three public forecasting benchmarks.

data.title: Tempo 3.1 Release: Kafka, Trace Redaction, and TraceQL Metrics
data.summary: Grafana Tempo 3.1 makes Kafka-backed tracing easier to run with TLS, additional authentication methods, rack-aware reads, and configurable producer compression. Query-based redaction can permanently remove sensitive trace data without enumerating trace IDs, while sampling-aware TraceQL metrics improve analysis of incomplete telemetry. Operators should use redaction dry-runs and complete the upgrade before applying time-bounded deletions.

data.title: AI in Production: Panellists Highlight Silent Failures, Harness Engineering, and Agent Governance
data.summary: Agentic systems can fail while conventional telemetry stays green: semantic drift can corrupt business meaning, and an embedding-model update can abruptly change policy decisions. Production controls therefore need continuous evals fed by live edge cases, separate agent identities with tiered permissions, and human approval of business risk. Treating agents as ordinary application code or relying on prompts for security leaves blind spots.

data.title: Reliable GPU compute for large training & inference jobs
data.summary: Large GPU jobs fail for many small infrastructure reasons, so reliability has to be continuous rather than reactive. Netflix built a layered system that validates nodes before jobs start, monitors hardware during runs, and automatically drains, reboots, resets, or replaces bad machines. The result is more usable GPU capacity and fewer long training or inference runs lost to platform faults.

data.title: Neon now has realtime

Unlike traditional SaaS pricing based on seats or transactions, AI costs depend on the complexity of each task and the resources needed to complete it. Companies must make usage limits and costs easier to understand while managing unpredictable computing expenses and preventing abuse of free plans.
